scope: Improve public-time support for every affected pre-reveal claim without changing the frozen five-card selection, market, dataset, measurement profile, or numeric anchors.

rules: A local capture retrieval time proves the bytes captured now, not historical publication.
A page's publisher metadata or a broadcast transcript timestamp is recorded as public-by evidence only unless it independently proves first distribution.
Official court PDFs, docket entries, and advisories establish dated substance and procedural status; their current upload time is not treated as the original public time.

The Supreme Court transcript and CNN live transcript are separate evidence: the former establishes the proceeding chronology, while the latter supplies a contemporaneous public broadcast passage before the retained 17:38Z cutoff.
No archive upload time, editable-page update, PDF filename timestamp, or current HTTP metadata is promoted to an original public fact.

remainingUnavailableEvidence: Exact first-public web posting times for the Dec. 6 opinion, Dec. 18 order, and Dec. 27 brief remain unavailable in the captured primary records. The v4 candidate therefore uses conservative public-by semantics rather than claiming exact first-public times.
The AP race-call publisher timestamp and CNN broadcast timestamp establish historical public artifacts/passages but not the first distribution channel.
A human editor must still approve the exact v4 field patch, wording, source roles, study version, content hash, and release timestamp.
